classification_signals: The paper describes a specific 'project created in an academic setting' (Abstract, p.2).
It details 'the process and results from the projects, which took place in 2019' (p.3).
It outlines the methodology involving 'emotion-sensing UpMood bracelets that collect biodata from the user' (p.2, p.8).
It explicitly states 'This project evaluates the use of these converging technologies' (p.2).
The 'findings of this process come in the form of data collected by the wearable technology from user feedback' (p.11).
The paper refers to 'our experiments with this project' (p.9).
title: Multi-sensory Materiality – Expanding Human Experience and Material Potentials with Advanced HoloLens Technologies and Emotion Sensing Wearables

minimum_safe_summary: This paper presents an empirical case study exploring multi-sensory materiality through an augmented reality installation. It investigates how advanced HoloLens technologies combined with emotion-sensing wearables can expand human sensory experience and material potentials in architectural design. Key findings indicate that multi-sensory interactions enhance material perception, lead to different spatial perceptions and embodied experiences, and that AR can increase awareness of material enhancements. The study also observed discrepancies between self-reported emotions and physiological data from wearables, which, while offering unique insights, were limited by the sensitivity of the data collection devices. The authors propose a new theoretical agenda for integrating technology into architectural design for deeper human experiences.
